issues.description: The problem specification (UML and description) requires a no-argument method checkOrderReady(): void that is invoked from orderMeal(), but the provided solution implements checkOrderReady with a boolean parameter (checkOrderReady(boolean)) and calls it with checkOrderReady(true). This deviates from the specified signature and may confuse students about the required method signature and how to call it.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the solution conform to the specification by providing a no-argument checkOrderReady() method. Either remove the boolean parameter and update internal logging accordingly, or add an overloaded no-arg checkOrderReady() that delegates to the existing method (e.g., public void checkOrderReady() { checkOrderReady(false); }) and ensure orderMeal() calls the no-arg variant as specified.

issues.description: The problem statement specifies a parameterless method checkOrderReady(): void (SealSaloon) in the class diagram, but the solution implements checkOrderReady with a boolean parameter (checkOrderReady(boolean enableLogging)). This divergence in the method signature (presence of an extra parameter) breaks the one-to-one mapping between the diagram/spec and the concrete implementation and may confuse students about the required method API and how orderMeal should invoke it.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the public checkOrderReady method match the specification by providing a parameterless checkOrderReady(): void. If a debug flag is needed internally, add a private overloaded method (e.g., checkOrderReady(boolean enableLogging)) or keep the debug parameter but do not expose it in the public API; update orderMeal to call the parameterless version so the implementation aligns clearly with the problem diagram.
